newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: LionOre says Australia nickel mine shines.
newsitem.headline: LionOre says Australia nickel mine shines.

text.p: Canada-based LionOre Mining International Ltd said that infill drilling at the Maggie Hays nickel project in Western Australia had returned one of the best nickel sulphide intersections achieved to date.

Diamond drilling intersected 37.58 metres of nickel mineralization at an average grade of 2.55 percent nickel, which includes 17.74 metres of mainly massive sulphides at a grade of 3.31 percent nickel, the company said in a statement released in Canada on Tuesday.
Maggie Hays is being developed by Perth-based Forrestania Gold NL, 98.5 percent-owned by LionOre.
Infill diamond drilling on the Maggie Hays deposit was aimed at better defining the internal continuity, grade and tonnage of the thicker, high grade central portion of the deposit, LionOre said.
Maggie Hays had an indicated resource as of December 1996 of 13.4 million tonnes grading 1.50 percent nickel, based on a 0.7 percent nickel cut-off grade.
